meta.title: Modern compound bow ontology
meta.purpose: Formal, build-ready description of a modern compound bow: part taxonomy, interfaces, and the cam-and-cable mechanics that make it compound. Drives a parametric 3D model (geometry authored, physics a readout) and a verification step.

reference.rationale: Current flagship hunting compound with a modular Crosscentric/SwitchWeight-X cam system, split limbs and a forged riser; published specs are complete.

units.mass: lb avoirdupois; arrow mass in grain (7000 gr = 1 lb)

provenance.published: Manufacturer/retailer spec sheet for the reference model.
provenance.classTypical: Typical of modern 30-34 in ATA compounds; not model-specific. Replace with measurement/CAD when authoring geometry.
provenance.derived: Computed from other values by the stated formula.

amoDrawLength.definition: AMO draw length = distance from string at full draw to the lowest point of the grip + 1.75 in.

braceHeight.definition: Distance from the grip pivot point (deepest point of the throat) to the string at rest.
braceHeight.note: Shorter brace = longer power stroke, less forgiving; longer brace = more forgiving, slightly slower.

ataSpeed.definition: ATA speed: initial velocity of a 350 gr arrow at 70 +/- 0.2 lb peak and 30 +/- 0.25 in draw length.

iboSpeed.definition: IBO speed: initial velocity of a 5 gr-per-lb arrow.
iboSpeed.note: Usually reported at 70 lb / 30 in; standard permits up to 80 +/- 2 lb and fixes no draw length.

minArrowMass.definition: Shoot at least 5 gr per lb of peak draw weight; lighter risks a dry-fire-like failure.

storedEnergyRatio.definition: Stored energy / peak draw force (Mullaney). Usually near 1.0, up to ~1.4 ft.lb/lb.

efficiency.definition: Stored energy transferred to the arrow.

classes.label: Bow
classes.definition: A device that stores elastic energy in limbs and transfers it to an arrow.

classes.label: Compound bow
classes.definition: A bow using cable-and-eccentric leverage to bend stiff limbs, with a force-draw curve that peaks early and lets off near full draw.

classes.label: Riser
classes.definition: Central rigid platform; carries limbs, grip, rest, sight, stabilizer and quiver.

classes.label: Riser body
classes.definition: Machined or forged main body with a sight window and structural bridges.

classes.label: Sight window
classes.definition: Arrow pass-through cutaway above the shelf that sets the limb-plane offset.

classes.label: Bridge
classes.definition: Flared web stiffening the riser in torsion; 'dual-bridged' risers have one above the sight window and one below the stabilizer insert.

classes.label: Grip
classes.definition: Hand interface; sets the pivot point. Modern one-piece polymer grips have a forward angle to reduce torque.

classes.label: Dovetail rest mount
classes.definition: Integrated dovetail that a compatible drop-away rest clamps into for alignment without bolts.

classes.label: Stabilizer bushing
classes.definition: Threaded insert (typically 5/16-24) below the grip for stabilizers and front bars.

classes.label: Accessory bushing
classes.definition: Threaded insert (quiver, wrist sling, sight).

classes.label: Limb
classes.definition: Elastic beam storing energy; flexed indirectly by cables pulling its tips toward each other.

classes.label: Split limb
classes.definition: Limb made of two parallel halves, giving a wide torsionally rigid footprint and a central cam slot.

classes.label: Limb pocket
classes.definition: Riser-mounted socket that holds the limb butt and sets its angle and stance.

classes.label: Limb bolt / tiller bolt
classes.definition: Threaded bolt through the pocket that sets limb preload (draw weight) and tiller; often 1/2-20.

classes.label: Limb retention
classes.definition: Clip/screw gripping the limb butt in the pocket for alignment and to keep the limb captive without drawing.

classes.label: Limb damper
classes.definition: Elastomer fitted to the limb that dissipates post-shot vibration.

classes.label: Eccentric
classes.definition: Non-concentric pulley that changes the string/cable moment arm as it rotates.

classes.label: Cam
classes.definition: Driven eccentric at a limb tip; grooves hold string and cables and its profile shapes the force-draw curve.

classes.label: Idler wheel
classes.definition: Round (concentric) wheel on one limb tip used in single-cam designs; routes the string with no energy storage.

classes.label: Cam module
classes.definition: Interchangeable plate that sets draw length, let-off and peak weight (e.g. Mathews SwitchWeight). Swapping it retunes the bow.

classes.label: Advanced Vectoring System disc
classes.definition: Small disc on a Crosscentric cam mounted offset to the axle and anchored to a harness-cable end; rotates non-concentrically to shift the force vector, storing more energy early and increasing let-off late.

classes.label: Draw stop
classes.definition: Post or peg that contacts a limb/cable at full draw, producing the solid back wall; adjustable to fine-tune draw length.

classes.label: Axle
classes.definition: Shaft through the limb tip on which the cam/idler rotates; its centres define axle-to-axle length.

classes.label: Bearing
classes.definition: Rolling or plain bearing between cam and axle for low-friction rotation.

classes.label: Cam spacer / shim
classes.definition: Thin washer setting cam centring and clearance in the limb slot.

classes.label: Cable
classes.definition: Low-stretch cord that couples the eccentrics to the limbs and synchronises them.

classes.label: Buss cable
classes.definition: Cable anchored to a cam and to the opposite limb (single-cam/hybrid designs).

classes.label: Harness / control cable
classes.definition: Cable spanning opposite cam anchors; its length and the cam rotation it induces set timing and let-off.

classes.label: Bowstring
classes.definition: Primary cord the archer draws; runs in the cam string grooves.

classes.label: Serving
classes.definition: Wound thread protecting the string at the centre and loops.

classes.label: D-loop
classes.definition: Loop tied on the centre serving that the release aid clips to.

classes.label: Nocking point
classes.definition: Set of knots that locate the arrow nock on the string.

classes.label: Cable guard
classes.definition: Bar that holds cables clear of the arrow's path.

classes.label: Roller guard
classes.definition: Guard with a roller that lets cables roll with reduced friction.

classes.label: Cable slide
classes.definition: Sliding block that keeps the two harness cables separated and parallel.

classes.label: Arrow
classes.definition: Shaft with nock, fletching and point; the payload.

classes.label: Fletching
classes.definition: Vanes that stabilise arrow flight.

classes.label: Arrow rest
classes.definition: Supports the arrow and drops away on release (drop-away) for clean flight.

classes.label: Sight
classes.definition: Pins and housing for aiming.

classes.label: Peep
classes.definition: Rear aperture served into the string, aligned with the sight.

classes.label: Stabilizer
classes.definition: Forward/side rods and weights that damp and steady the bow.

classes.label: String stop
classes.definition: Riser-mounted rubber bumper that arrests the string after the shot, cutting noise and vibration.

classes.label: String silencer
classes.definition: Fuzzy elastomer tufts (e.g. Monkey Tails) served onto the string.

classes.label: Release aid
classes.definition: Mechanical trigger/tension release clipped to the D-loop for a consistent loose.

classes.label: Feature
classes.definition: A named region of a part rather than a separate part.

classes.label: Interface
classes.definition: A mounting feature that accepts a standardised accessory.

classes.label: Limb half
classes.definition: One of the two parallel beams of a split limb.

classes.label: Draw stroke
classes.definition: The nock travel from brace to the wall; what the draw stop terminates.

classes.label: Force vector
classes.definition: Direction and magnitude of the cable force acting on a cam.

classes.label: Draw-length setting
classes.definition: The draw length selected by a cam module.

materials.label: Forged aluminium
materials.note: Forging improves toughness vs. billet machining.

subsystems.label: Riser platform
subsystems.function: Rigid reference frame carrying every load; sight window sets arrow pass and limb-plane offset.

subsystems.label: Energy-storage limbs
subsystems.function: Elastic beams bent by cable tension; store the shot energy and return it.

subsystems.label: Eccentric / let-off system
subsystems.function: Change moment arm through the draw to store energy early and let off late; provide the solid wall.

subsystems.label: String and cable train
subsystems.function: Couple the cams to the limbs and to each other; deliver force to the arrow.

subsystems.label: Arrow and aiming
subsystems.function: Support, aim and launch the projectile; hold and release the string consistently.

frames.note: Right-handed bow, looking at the archer's side.

axes.x: +x = forward, along the arrow (away from the archer)
axes.z: +z = toward the archer's face (string side); arrow pass is at +z of the riser face

datums.definition: Deepest point of the grip throat; origin for brace height and AMO draw length.
Centre of the upper cam axle; locates the top of the ATA span.
Centre of the lower cam axle.
Plane containing the bowstring at brace; brace height is pivotPoint to this plane.
Point the arrow leaves the rest; roughly the top of the grip shelf.
Point where the arrow nocks; draw length is measured to this.

mechanics.summary: The limbs store the energy; the eccentrics and cables decide how hard and how long you must pull to load them, and how little you must hold at full draw. The bow is drawn by cables pulling the limb tips TOWARD EACH OTHER, not by the string bending the limbs backward.

eccentricTopologies.label: Single cam + idler
eccentricTopologies.definition: One driven cam (usually lower) and one round idler wheel. The string runs from the cam over the idler; a buss cable ties the cam to the opposite limb.
traits: nock travels on a shallow arc

eccentricTopologies.label: Hybrid cam
eccentricTopologies.definition: Two eccentrics controlled by one cable; the second cam is often a control cam rather than a mirrored drive cam.

eccentricTopologies.label: Dual cam
eccentricTopologies.definition: Two mirrored cams, each with its own cable anchored to the limb or cam.
traits: can be tuned for nock travel

eccentricTopologies.label: Binary cam
eccentricTopologies.definition: Two mirrored cams; each cable is anchored to the OPPOSITE cam, so the pair is self-correcting and stays synchronised. No cable is anchored to a limb.
traits: needs precise cable lengths and cam-to-cam timing

eccentricTopologies.label: Quad cam
eccentricTopologies.definition: Two cams with multiple tracks; mechanically a binary variant with additional take-up.

eccentricTopologies.label: Hinged / limb-mounted eccentric
eccentricTopologies.definition: Eccentric carried on a hinged link rather than directly on the limb tip; uncommon.

referenceEccentricSystem.label: Crosscentric cam with Advanced Vectoring System and SwitchWeight-X modules
principle: The cam is non-circular: its effective radius (the moment arm from the axle to the string/cable contact) changes as it rotates, so a roughly constant cable tension produces a shaped draw-force curve.

The AVS uses two small discs per cam mounted OFFSET to the axle and anchored to the ends of the harness cable. As they rotate non-concentrically they shift the force vector, storing more energy at the front of the draw and increasing let-off at the back.
The SwitchWeight module is the interface between the module and the cam tracks; swapping it changes draw length, let-off (80 or 85%) and peak weight in steps without changing limbs.
The draw stop on each cam strikes the limb at full draw, giving a hard back wall and fixing the anchor; its position also trims draw length.

drawCycle.note: Cam rotation and lever-arm change are read from the reference mechanism photograph (commons_cam_forcedraw.jpg): five poses at 0, 45, 90, 135 and ~210 degrees of rotation, annotated with lever arms and the cable take-up length.

phases.force: brace preload (small, set by limb tiller)
phases.behaviour: String at rest at the brace height; cables pre-tensioned; limbs already bent from their moulded shape.

phases.force: rises steeply to the peak within the first third
phases.behaviour: Cams turn and their long moment arms load the limbs hard; this is where a compound stores most of its energy per inch.

phases.force: roughly flat near the peak ('stacking' if it rises, 'soft' if it falls)
phases.behaviour: The effective radius stays high; the archer does most of the work but feels an even pull.

phases.force: falls sharply toward the holding weight
phases.behaviour: The moment arm collapses as the string approaches the axle; stored energy is nearly maximum while the force needed falls.
Draw stop contacts the limb; a hard, repeatable stop. The archer stops pulling.

phases.force: limb torque drives the cams back
phases.behaviour: The cables unwind the cams; the limbs pull the string forward and launch the arrow.

storedEnergy.formula: E_stored = integral F(s) ds over the power stroke
storedEnergy.note: The area under the force-draw curve; the reason a compound stores more than a recurve of equal peak weight.

arrowKinetic.formula: KE = 0.5 * m * v^2 / gc, gc = 32.174 lb.ft/(lbf.s^2)

iboCheck.note: Sanity bound: IBO figures are optimistic and measured at 70 lb peak, so the implied stored/peak ratio sits above the 1.0-1.4 class-typical band. The model must not treat 343 fps as a guaranteed delivered speed.

synchronisation.definition: Both cams must reach the wall together and stay in phase through the draw; if they drift, the nock travels off-axis and accuracy suffers.
mechanisms: timing marks on cam and limb
cam-to-cam cable anchors on binary cams self-correct
synchronisation.observable: nock travel: the path of the nock relative to the arrow pass.

forceVectoring.definition: Offset discs alter the direction as well as the magnitude of the cable force on the cam, changing how much energy is stored early and how much the force drops late.

states.label: Brace / at rest
states.description: String at brace height; limbs pre-bent by cable tension; no draw force on the string beyond preload.

states.label: Drawing
states.description: String pulled back; cams rotate and cables load the limbs; force rises along the F-d curve.

states.label: Peak weight
states.description: Maximum force early in the draw.

states.label: Let-off / valley
states.description: Force falls as the effective moment arm collapses.

states.label: Wall / full draw
states.description: Draw stops bear on the limbs; holding weight is 15-20% of peak; the archer anchors.

states.label: Release
states.description: Release aid fires; cables unwind; limbs drive the string forward.

states.label: Recovery
states.description: String is arrested by the string stop; dampers and string silencers dissipate vibration; cams return to brace.

buildPhases.label: Riser platform
buildPhases.note: The rigid frame every later part references.

buildPhases.label: Limb pockets and limbs
buildPhases.note: Limbs pivot in the pockets and are preloaded by the tiller bolts.

buildPhases.label: Axles, bearings, cams, modules, AVS, draw stops
buildPhases.note: Cams go in the limb slots on bearings; modules and draw stops set draw length and wall.

buildPhases.label: String and cables
buildPhases.note: Requires a bow press: limbs must be compressed to relieve cable tension.

buildPhases.label: Timing and tuning
buildPhases.note: Set cam timing, draw length, let-off and tiller; verify with timing marks.

buildPhases.label: Dampers, string furniture, accessories
buildPhases.note: Everything the archer touches, plus the projectile.
